title: HR tech’s next move: Winning wireless
summary: As product teams at leading HR tech companies race to answer that question, one major pain point is suddenly attracting a lot of attention:…
body_text: Few technologies have attracted as much investor attention in recent years as HR tech. Take Deel : in just five years, it hit a $12 billion valuation with over $500 million in annual recurring revenue. And it’s not alone. With Gusto worth $9.5 billion, Remote over $3 billion, and Rippling now $13.5 billion, the HR tech space is flush with fresh venture capital. What’s driving this trend is the growing demand for all-in-one platforms which consolidate HR software with adjacent functions like compliance and finance. In the early days, Rippling focused on easing employee onboarding. Since then, it has expanded into an end-to-end employee management platform, covering everything from payroll to mobile device management. More established players like Workday have gone down a similar route, offering customers a one-stop shop to manage finance, HR, and spend on a global scale. The message is clear: Why juggle a dozen systems to handle the employee lifecycle when one platform can do it all? The next innovation in HR As the HR tech space grows increasingly competitive, leading platforms are developing ever more innovative ways to streamline corporate workflows. The most successful players have zeroed in on the inefficiencies impacting modern teams, offering digital solutions that make complex tasks intuitive. Take payroll, for example. Not long ago, businesses accepted that paying employees required a complex web of systems and manual processes. HR Platforms like Rippling and Gusto have flipped the switch on that narrative so effectively that older payroll systems now feel woefully outdated. In addition to payroll, they both now offer employer of record (EOR) solutions as an extension to their core business, allowing companies to hire and manage talent efficiently, both domestically and internationally. They've also streamlined expense management, automated bill pay, and simplified employee benefits. So, what’s the next workplace process in dire need of an overhaul? As product teams at leading HR tech companies race to answer that question, one major pain point is suddenly attracting a lot of attention: Employee phone plans. Corporate connectivity: A long overlooked opportunity For many companies, managing employee phone plans is a major hassle. I’ve seen teams struggle with over 4,000 employee phone plans across 20+ carriers and countries. This isn’t just a high-cost, high-maintenance logistical challenge—it also raises significant security and compliance risks, potentially exposing organizations to major liabilities. In most companies, employee SIM cards are still shipped by mail, exposing organizations to the serious risk of identity fraud. Meanwhile, the absence of programmatic SIM management creates blind spots for IT teams, leaving businesses under threat from SIM swap fraud and other telecom scams. Imagine if keeping employees connected was as simple and secure as paying them. It's a problem that HR platforms are primed to solve. Just picture this: One contract and invoice for employee phone plans across carriers and countries. Seamless onboarding: New hires receive their eSIM by email or Slack, connect in seconds, and are ready to go. A connectivity dashboard: Where employers can assign role-specific phone plans for team members and monitor usage. A simple interface: Where employees can request travel eSIMs for work trips with a click. Effortless offboarding: When employees leave, their eSIM deactivates automatically—no termination fees, no security risks, no hassle. The rise of embedded connectivity In the past, embedding a mobile offering into an HR platform would be a huge undertaking, requiring vast amounts of capital, time, and developer resources. But today, that’s all changed. Much as Stripe simplified payments back in the day, API-based connectivity platforms have removed the regulatory and technical complexity of offering mobile services. With the right telecom partner, platforms can integrate multi-carrier phone plans seamlessly into their product in just a few weeks, instantly unlocking a new revenue stream that turns a profit from Day One. The embedded connectivity movement has seen several tech players—from fintech giants like Nubank to cell phone brands like Light —enter the telecom game. But, so far, workplace phone plans remain an untapped market. One with huge potential. With businesses spending upwards of $1000 per employee per year on mobile enablement, there are few products that can match the potential upside of connectivity. Platform stickiness: Wireless is a notoriously sticky product. Once a business has moved their employees onto a single solution, they’re unlikely to switch. Product differentiation: Phone plans are currently a unique selling point in the hotly contested HR tech market. Global scale: Multi-carrier APIs allow platforms to launch local phone plans and travel eSIMs on a global scale with one simple integration. Recurring revenue: HR platforms can earn recurring revenue from each connected line. With every enterprise client needing thousands of employee plans, that’s a massive revenue boost. What’s more, by upselling mobile plans to existing customers, HR platforms can drive additional revenue at zero acquisition cost and minimal cost to serve. The missing piece The ability to seamlessly provision and manage employee eSIMs isn't just a convenience, it's a fundamental requirement for today's workforce. As well as managing phone plans for office-based employees, many companies are now supporting frequent travelers and hybrid workers who need reliable connectivity wherever they go. With Gigs’ OS, HR platforms can embed enterprise-grade phone plans seamlessly into their core services and allow their customers to configure, provision, and manage premium phone plans in 50 countries and travel data in 195 countries. HR tech platforms have already transformed the way companies hire, compensate, and reward their employees, streamlining workflows and accelerating the digital economy. Telecom is the final missing piece. Early movers will have a significant advantage—capturing market share, delivering added value to customers, and capitalizing on this vast untapped opportunity.

title: Middle School Student Strength Survey Questions
summary: Learn how to create effective middle school student strength surveys that uncover hidden talents, improve teaching strategies, and build confidence. Includes actionable questions and implementation tips.
body_text: Middle School Student Strength Surveys: A Guide to Empowering Students and Teachers Middle school marks a crucial transition in a student's educational journey. It's when young minds begin to shape their identities, discover their interests, and develop learning preferences that can influence their academic future. Understanding student strengths during this pivotal time isn't just helpful—it's essential for creating an environment where every student can thrive. ‍ Understanding the Impact of Strength Identification When we identify student strengths early, we open doors to personalized learning paths that extend far beyond middle school. Think of strength identification as planting seeds for future growth. These insights help students discover their interests, build confidence, and make informed decisions about their academic journey. Teachers who understand their students' strengths can create more engaging lessons, foster better connections, and support students in ways that resonate with their natural abilities. This understanding transforms the classroom from a one-size-fits-all environment into a space where diverse talents flourish. ‍ Creating Effective Survey Questions The key to gathering meaningful insights lies in asking the right questions. Here's a comprehensive guide to crafting questions that reveal student strengths across different dimensions: ‍ Academic Strengths Assessment Core subject questions that reveal competencies and interests: Mathematics "Rate your confidence in the following math areas (1-5 scale): Problem-solving Mental calculations Geometric concepts Data interpretation" "Which math topics make you most excited to learn about?" "How do you prefer to approach challenging math problems?" Science "Which of these science activities do you enjoy most?" Conducting experiments Analyzing data Making predictions Explaining concepts to others "What types of scientific questions make you curious?" "How comfortable are you with designing your own experiments?" Language Arts "What types of writing do you enjoy most?" Creative stories Persuasive essays Research papers Personal narratives "How do you approach understanding complex reading passages?" "What strategies help you remember new vocabulary?" ‍ Learning Style and Preferences Questions to understand how students best process information: Visual Learning "Do diagrams and charts help you understand new concepts?" "How often do you draw pictures to solve problems?" "What role do visual aids play in your note-taking?" Auditory Learning "How well do you learn from classroom discussions?" "Do you prefer verbal or written instructions?" "How often do you explain concepts to others to understand them better?" Hands-on Learning "What types of hands-on activities help you learn best?" "How do you prefer to practice new skills?" "What role does physical movement play in your learning?" ‍ Social-Emotional Skills Questions to assess interpersonal abilities and emotional intelligence: Collaboration "What role do you usually take in group projects?" "How do you help resolve conflicts in group settings?" "What makes you feel most supported when working with others?" Leadership "How comfortable are you leading class discussions?" "What leadership opportunities interest you most?" "How do you help others succeed in group work?" Problem-Solving "What strategies do you use when facing challenging assignments?" "How do you overcome obstacles in your learning?" "What resources do you seek when you need help?" ‍ Interest and Motivation Questions to uncover passions and drive: Future Goals "What subjects make you lose track of time?" "What topics would you like to learn more about?" "What kind of projects would you create if given free choice?" Learning Environment "When do you feel most engaged in class?" "What classroom activities make learning most enjoyable?" "How do you prefer to show what you've learned?" ‍ Self-Reflection Questions that promote metacognition: Growth Mindset "How do you view mistakes in your learning journey?" "What strategies help you improve in challenging subjects?" "How do you measure your own progress?" These questions serve as a foundation and can be customized based on specific school contexts and student populations. Using an AI-powered survey platform can help generate relevant follow-up questions based on initial responses, creating a more dynamic and insightful assessment process. ‍ Implementing Surveys Effectively Timing matters when conducting strength surveys. The beginning of the school year provides baseline information, while mid-year assessments can track growth and adjust support strategies. Tools like Aftercare streamline this process by automatically generating relevant survey questions based on your needs - simply describe what insights you're looking for, and AI creates a comprehensive survey in seconds. This saves valuable time that can be better spent analyzing and acting on the results. Create a supportive environment where students feel comfortable sharing honest feedback. Explain how their responses will help teachers better support their learning journey. Modern survey tools can adapt question phrasing based on age appropriateness and reading levels, ensuring clear communication. ‍ Leveraging Technology for Deeper Insights Modern survey platforms like Aftercare use AI to transform static questionnaires into dynamic conversations. When a student indicates interest in a particular subject, Aftercare automatically generates relevant follow-up questions to understand the specific aspects that capture their attention. For instance, if a student mentions enjoying science experiments, the AI immediately asks about their favorite types of experiments or what aspects of the scientific method they find most engaging. This adaptive approach yields richer insights than traditional fixed surveys. For example, if a student expresses interest in science experiments, an AI-powered survey might explore whether they enjoy the hypothesis formation, the hands-on testing, or the data analysis aspects most. This granular understanding helps teachers design more engaging lessons and suggest relevant extracurricular activities. ‍ Creating an Inclusive Learning Environment Survey insights help teachers create more inclusive classrooms where different types of intelligence are recognized and celebrated. When teachers understand that some students process information visually while others prefer hands-on learning, they can diversify their teaching approaches accordingly. This understanding extends beyond academic subjects. Recognizing and validating different communication styles, problem-solving approaches, and creative expressions helps build a classroom culture where every student feels valued. ‍ Building Future Pathways Middle school strength surveys lay groundwork for future academic and career exploration. When students understand their strengths early, they make more informed decisions about high school courses and extracurricular activities. Teachers can use survey insights to: Recommend relevant advanced learning opportunities Suggest complementary extracurricular activities Guide course selection for high school Connect students with mentorship programs Identify potential career paths that align with student interests ‍ Supporting Student Growth Understanding student strengths doesn't mean ignoring areas for improvement. Instead, it provides context for developing effective support strategies. When students struggle with certain subjects, knowing their strengths helps teachers frame challenges in more accessible ways. For example, a student who excels in creative writing but struggles with math might benefit from word problems that incorporate storytelling elements. This strength-based approach to addressing challenges helps maintain student confidence while building new skills. ‍ Moving Forward with Student Strength Assessment The landscape of student assessment continues to evolve, with technology making it easier to gather and act on meaningful insights. Platforms like Aftercare transform the traditional survey process by: Automatically generating personalized surveys based on your needs Asking intelligent follow-up questions to uncover deeper insights Analyzing open-ended responses to identify common themes and patterns Creating visual summaries that make data immediately actionable Providing an AI chat interface for Pro users to analyze and query survey results This technological evolution means educators can spend less time on survey creation and data analysis, and more time implementing insights to support student growth. By understanding and nurturing student strengths during the middle school years, we set the stage for success in high school and beyond. The key lies in asking the right questions, interpreting responses effectively, and using those insights to create supportive learning environments where every student can thrive.
